question: Pursuant to Regulation (EU) 2019/2144, each child restraint system (CRS) must be subjected to analyses and crash tests in independent laboratories in order to be approved. These tests must be scientific and repeatable, and the results should be standardised and mutually comparable. The results are held by the manufacturers of CRS equipment.

Although these results relate to the basic safety function of CRS equipment, they are not made available to consumers, even in truncated form. As a result, when purchasing CRS equipment, consumers do not have objective, comparable data assessing the level of safety. Could the Commission therefore answer the following questions: 1.
What actions and measures has the Commission implemented to address this problem?

Is the Commission considering the introduction of mandatory information on the results of typeapproval tests for CRS appliances, e.g. in a form similar to the energy labels applied to and required for refrigerators and freezers under Regulation (EU) 2019/2016 or for tyres under Regulation (EU) 2020/740?
answer: Regulation (EU) 2019/2144 (1) lays down technical requirements for the approval of child restraint system to be fitted in motor vehicles with the view of their placing on the Single Market. The requirements are performance-based and the outcome of the tests is either ‘pass’ or ‘fail’.

It is not the objective of the type-approval framework to compare a product and its performance vis-à-vis other products on the market. Such activities fall within the remit of consumer organisations with the view to provide informative choice for endusers.

There is no legal base in the EU type-approval legislation for introducing mandatory information requirements on the results of type-approval tests or for performance labels for automotive products in general and for child restraint systems, in particular. Hence, the Commission is not considering any legislative proposal in this respect.

Regulation (EU) 2019/2144 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 27 November 2019 on type-approval requirements for motor vehicles and their trailers, and systems, components and separate technical units intended for such vehicles, as regards their general safety and the protection of vehicle occupants and vulnerable road users, OJ L 325, 16.12.2019, p.1-40.
